corrections.reason: The proposal records the answers to Q1 to Q16 and the acceptance of N1 to N3 under 'Owner answers', with the alternatives kept as options considered; no question remains open. Q1: the identity document number is identified by a fixed field kind and always masked with the fixed rule, with no Strapi masking option (AC-069, AC-090, AC-094, AC-095). Q13: leaving while a payment is processed asks first with the leave confirmations of AC-033 and AC-034, using its own copy (new AC-096; AC-073, AC-078, AC-089, AC-090 to AC-093). Q15: CAP-002 is a base at its integrated revision and REQ-009 is revised to retire AC-066, so AC-082 is the only statement of the public role; because a revised requirement needs a new acceptance criterion, REQ-009 gains AC-097 (the final price is requested without a token). Q16: dependencies on CAP-001 and CAP-002, both integrated.

derived.reason: The story names the summary's elements but not their copy; the engineering reference requires all user-facing copy to come from Strapi except the fallback, as AC-008 and AC-040 do for the earlier steps, and missing copy must be invalid content (P3).

The story says the person views the terms but not how; the design reference places a terms link below the call to action and requires keyboard operation, visible focus and no traps, so the dialog's focus, closing and scrolling must be stated.

The story has no loading, unavailable, missing or duplicated terms case; principle P3, the architecture (terms are read with the country's content) and the gap checklist (Strapi unavailable, content not published) require controlled states, as AC-015 to AC-017 and AC-059 do.

The story does not say what leaves the browser to pay; principles P4 and P5, the engineering reference (personal data is not logged) and AC-026 and AC-046 require the minimum: country and plan only, nothing stored or logged by the stateless endpoint.

The story needs terms and a payment endpoint but says nothing about access; principle P4 and the architecture limit the public role to read actions on wizard content types plus the two custom endpoints, with no token in the browser.

The story does not say what happens when the person returns to earlier steps after paying; without a rule the person could pay the same quote twice or lose the confirmation, and AC-020 and AC-053 keep earlier steps navigable.

The story ends at the confirmation and does not say how a person quotes again in the same tab; the wizard data is kept per tab (AC-023), so without an explicit action the paid quote would stay on every visit.

The story does not cover reloading or leaving the summary; the gap checklist requires stating reload and navigation, and CHG-001's leave confirmation (AC-033, AC-034) needs a statement for this step when no payment is processed, as AC-057 gives for the plan step.
The story has no accessibility criteria; principle P6 and the design reference require programmatic names, associations, announced states and an automated scan in every state.
The story has no accessibility criteria; the design reference requires keyboard-only completion with visible focus and no traps, checked in every user interface review.
The story has no responsive criteria; the design reference sets the reference widths, reflow to 320 px without horizontal scrolling and the minimum target size.
The story has no motion criteria; the design reference requires respecting the reduced-motion preference.

The story does not cover leaving while a payment is processed; the owner answered Q13 that leaving then asks first, reusing the leave confirmations of AC-033 and AC-034, so the behavior, its copy and the browsers without the native confirmation must be stated.

Retiring AC-066 (owner answer Q15) revises REQ-009, which needs a new acceptance criterion; AC-097 keeps the price-quote part of AC-066 (no token in the browser, P4), while AC-082 stays the only list of the public role's actions.
